samples.summary: `get` neuters inherited `Object.prototype` methods too, so stringifying or probing the handle misbehaves (`String(store)` throws)
samples.evidence: `get` returns `noop` for ANY function-valued property not in the allowlist, and `Reflect.get(target, prop)` walks the target's real prototype chain — so `toString`, `valueOf`, `toLocaleString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf` and `constructor` all resolve to `noop`. Consequences on a viewer mount: `` `${store}` `` / `String(store)` runs OrdinaryToPrimitive, gets `undefined` from both `toString()` and `valueOf()`, and throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`; `store.hasOwnProperty(x)` silently answers `undefined` (falsy) for every key; `store.constructor` is a no-op function (compounded by `getPrototypeOf: () => null`, which also makes `store instanceof YorkieNoteStore` false). Nothing in the notes engine interpolates or probes the handle today, so this is latent rather than firing now — but the neutering is meant to make writes inert, not to break value semantics, and a future log line / diagnostic / assertion that stringifies the store crashes only on read-only mounts. An `Object.prototype`-inherited passthrough (or restricting the noop to own/class-prototype members) would avoid it.

samples.summary: The non-configurable/non-writable escape hatch in `get` returns the RAW member, so the allowlist fails open for that property shape
samples.evidence: `if (own && own.configurable === false && own.writable === false) return own.value` short-circuits before the allowlist is consulted. If a store implementation ever defines a method (or a field holding the CRDT handle) as a non-configurable, non-writable own property — e.g. via `Object.defineProperty` in a constructor, or a bundler/decorator transform — the real, unneutered function is handed back and `editText`/`doc` become reachable on a viewer mount, while `has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` all still report it as present. The comment claims neither store has such a property today (true for `MemNoteStore` and `YorkieNoteStore`, which use ordinary class fields), so this is a latent fail-open in a construct whose whole documented premise is that it fails closed for members it does not know.
searchedFor: class field declarations in memory.ts / yorkie-note-store.ts

samples.summary: The store guard is chosen once at mount; `readOnly` is not an effect dependency, so a viewer→editor role change leaves a permanently write-neutered handle with no error
samples.evidence: `const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw;` lives inside the effect whose dep array is `[didMount, doc]` (line 174, with `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` disabled). `SharedNotesLayout` derives `readOnly` from `resolved.role` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:44), and `resolved` comes from a react-query result that can refetch; if the role flips viewer→editor without the Yorkie `doc` identity changing, the editor keeps the neutered proxy and every subsequent keystroke path is a silent no-op (writes swallowed, no user-visible failure). The pre-existing `EditorState.readOnly`/`changeFilter` staleness has the same shape, but this delta extends it to the store, i.e. to the CRDT write itself; adding `readOnly` to the dep list (or keying the mount on it) would make the two agree.

samples.summary: The `members` memo map is keyed by every property ever read through the proxy and is never pruned
samples.evidence: `members.set(prop, …)` caches an entry for any function-valued property access, including ones that are not `NoteStore` members (inherited `Object.prototype` methods, framework probes). The key set is bounded in practice by what code actually touches, so this is not a leak of consequence — noting it only because the map lives for the lifetime of the mount and grows with dynamically-named accesses.
